body: Galways land national park is a tiny 27 hectare national park situated within the Nuwara Eliya city limits. We've been visiting Nuwara Eliya for many years but never really got around to visiting this place. And even this time around we read all the discouraging reviews went elsewhere, but then decided to give it a try anyway since it was on our way and we had spare time....But we ended up thoroughly enjoying the half and hour cool and calm hike through the forest. I would even rate the experience 5 stars if it wasn't for comparing it with other hikes. I think the key is not to have too much expectationsand enjoying it for what it is ;) The notice says there are birds and deer. We saw one bird (a common one we've seen many times before) and an animal that may have been a deer... but having been to much larger national parks and how animal sightings work we didn't have any expectation of spotting any animals on a half an hour hike...On the plus side the park is within 5-10 minutes driving distance from the NE town, the roads are good, there is a bit of parking space, there is a pathway (paved upto a point), you can take a hike in cool climes without sweating buckets (which is a big thing for us local lowlanders ;) and the ticket for a local is around LKR 70. So if you want a quick change from the usual hustle and bustle of the NE city this is the ideal mood changer..... There are two treks. Almost as soon as you start there is a left turn which is the starting point of trek one, it ends after 850 meters but you would likely miss the small plaque that says so since the second trail just starts from that point. (But the first trail is paved while the second one is paved only for the first 100 meters or so and then at a latter point where there are steps.) The second trails continues for 1350 meters and ends at the place you started. There were only about 10 cement steps or so at one point, otherwise it was all flat land walking. The whole trail took about 35 minutes with photostops.The climate inside the park can be a couple of degrees cooler. We went on an overcast day but it wasn't dark or eerie as some other reviewers has suggested;) Plus the path actually runs parrarel to the boundaries of the park, so you could see other building etc most of the time.We couldn't check the price for foreigners but if they do charge LKR 3000-4000 as other reviews say, that definelty is a rip off as there isn't much effort put in by the authorities provide any facilities or to maintain the place expect for a couple of washrooms (which we didn't check out.)
title: A miniature hiking experience....

body: We decided to head over to this park having landed in Nuwara Eliya and having a couple of hours to spare in the afternoon. A short tuktuk ride later and we arrived to a quiet looking entrance and some bemused staff. Entry costs are steep for what it is - $10 plus tax per person. We headed in and realised pretty quickly we were the only ones there - and I'm not just talking about tourists, the wildlife seemed to be avoiding the place too! The route through the place is a 2km circular, and while the woodlands look like they should be a haven for wildlife there was pretty much nothing to see (or hear!) We wandered round, seeing the occasional bird, but nothing amazing. The highlight was a giant squirrel, but that was about it. Very little reward for $23 and a couple of hours. I guess that maybe we just timed it badly - we were there between 3 and 5pm - but it's hard to know. As such, I'm struggling to recommend it, but I'd certainly say, in my experience, it's not worth a trip late afternoon. Save your money and head up to the Horton Plains the next day instead!
title: Hard to know if it's any good or not, but avoid late-afternoon!

body: Galways Land is a small National Park close to the hill resort of Nuwara Elliya. It's a bit difficult to find your way if you drive on your own. Use Google maps or similar to get their easily. The best times to visit are the morning and evening. There's no facility to park a large number of vehicles inside the gate. Hoy,roadside parking is possible. There are two trails to take which together add up to 2 km. It's mostly a gentle gradient with the exception of several steps in a few locations. One should take both trails. It is a pleasure to walk inside the forest that has some very tall trees. Several species of animals native to Sri Lanka are found here. These include bird species and Rhino horned lizard. Barking deer is also found. However, don't expect to see many animals here as it's difficult to spot them. We only saw the Rhino Horned Lizard. It was a delight to this beautiful and rare species.
title: Excellent excursion in Nuwara Elliya

body: This is a newer park in Nuwara Eliya, so many locals aren't familiar with it's location. The price is bit steep at $10, but we really enjoyed the park and felt that it was worth it. The path through the forest is about 2km long and easy to follow. We saw several types of endemic birds and barking deer. The best time to go is early morning. Don't forget to bring your binoculars!

body: It's about 2.5 km hike along a narrow pathway. Some areas are paved with stones but some areas are muddy with slippery ground. Need good hiking shoes and a bottle of water. It is said that the forest is a habitat for some native birds and has posters indicating where you can see them.But on this day we didn't see a single bird. Only a lizard and a squirrel. There's a entrance fee and you are not provided a guide. If you don't have anything to do in Nuwara Eliya go there. Otherwise it is a waste of money and time.

body: Location Central province, Sri LankaNearest city Nuwara EliyaCoordinates 6°58′00″N 80°46′38″ECoordinates: 6°58′00″N 80°46′38″EArea 27 hectares (0.10 sq mi)[1]Established 1938 (Sanctuary)2006 (National park)Governing body Department of Wildlife Conservation Galway's Land National Park is a small national park situated within the city limits of Nuwara Eliya in Sri Lanka. Have been declared as a wildlife sanctuary on 27 May 1938. The Galway's Land was elevated to the national park status on 18 May 2006. The park was declared to conserve the montane ecosystems. Field Ornithology Group of Sri Lanka considers that the Victoria park of Nuwara Eliya and the Galway's Land as two of the most significant birding sites in Sri Lanka. Galway's Land harbours about 20 rare migrant bird species and 30 native species. Apart from the avifauna, the park has valuable floral species of both native and foreign origin. Galway Forest Lodge is located close to the park.
title: About PARK

body: We visited this reserve at around 12am. This is a very small bit of forest in the centre of Nuwara Eliy. Tickets are not cheap. The guy at the ticket desk told us it is 22 acres in total. Visitor walk along a 2 km cobbled loop around the park. The walk is monotonous and unexciting. The forest along the pass does not change much.Despite a few signed and boards describing various birds, deer, lizards that inhabit the park, we did not see any animals. In my opinion better to go twice to Horton Reserve instead.
title: Small and expencive place

body: This tiny gem of a NP offers a welcome escape from the heat and hustle of Nuwara Eliya. Armed with our binoculars and accompanied by our knowledgeable Sri lankan driver/guide we wandered round Galway's Land and had close encounters with a buffalo and a barking deer, both of which were surprised to see us, and saw several interesting birds despite the fact that we were there in the middle of the day. The paths were well marked and had helpful information boards on the local species. Paying £5 to Sri Lanka National Parks for the opportunity to get away from the mass of humanity seems like good value to us and infinitely preferable to Gregory's Lake and Victoria Park, but not the place for instant gratification.
title: A little gem

body: Galway's is a tiny National Park tucked away on the eastern outskirts of Nuwara Eliya. I visited mid morning and was very disappointed especially with the very high price and the absence of any meaningful information, although it was a very pleasant walk through the woods with a few interesting birds and animals to see if you were quiet and patient.The positives are:- Peaceful walk through towering forest - when I visited I was the first visitor they had all day, and some days nobody visits- Paths are mostly well made, but some unpaved sections will be muddy in the rain.The negatives are:- Difficult to find: We had to ask several people in different hotels, and tuk tuk drivers, before we found anybody who had even heard of it. For the record, it is beyond the wholesale veg market on the eastern edge of town, then look carefully for the signs that are almost faded to the point of illegibility. No wonder at best a handful of people visit it each day.- High price: for westerners it is US$10. The comments below about the "low price" are from locals who pay well under $1. - No information available. The only information available is a map at he entrance that has faded to a meaningless blue and black lines, and a series of small signs along the walks with random pictures and names of birds and animals that live there. There is no leaflet, or any sort of explanation boards anywhere. I don't mind contributing to supporting nature, but for western style entrance prices I expect an attempt an western style information.So basically, if you can find it you get a peaceful stroll through the woods with no idea what trees there are or where the deer normally live. Very disappointing, with a bit of investment and effort it could be so much more.
title: An expensive walk through the woods - could be so much more

body: The Galway Forest Reserve is one of a kind being located in the town environs of Nuwara Eliya about 30 hectares in extent is a must for bird lovers. It has a a dwindling herd of the elusive barking deer (you'll be lucky to spot them - quiet and patience pays). Rock squirrels, jungle fowl and several species of endemic and migrant bird species. An early morning visit is a rewarding experience well worth a visit and value for money for bird lovers.
title: One of a kind

body: Gallways Land NP is the smallest park situated within Nuwaraeliya town. You have to travel along Nuwaraeliya-Udupussallawa road and get the road behind economic center. There are well paved foot pathways inside this park. It takes 1-2 hours to walk there. If you are interested in bird watching you can spend more time. No camping facilities inside the park.

body: This is a small park close to Nuwara Eliya. You can take a 3-wheeler (ca. 150 Rs.) from the middle of town to take you there in 5 minutes. There is a nice walking path going in a circle through a small forest. We went there for birding and we indeed saw some interesting forest birds. We also spotted the rhino horned lizard, a barking deer, a shrew and some pretty butterflies. There are some benches along the path to take a break and there are also sign boards here and there, pointing out the animals you can find in the forest. The path is well maintained and there is no garbage lying around. We really enjoyed our walk.
